# Prayer-time oracle matrix — INPUT to test/unit/salah_oracle_spec.sh, never regenerated by a
# test run. Nothing here is a golden file: the expectations came from outside this repo.
#
# PROVENANCE
#
# The `oracle` column is what the public Aladhan API answered, fetched once by hand at the time
# this file was written. Every row is one request of the form
#
#   https://api.aladhan.com/v1/timings/DD-MM-YYYY
#     ?latitude=LAT&longitude=LON&timezonestring=TZ
#     &method=M&school=S&latitudeAdjustmentMethod=L
#
# with the method, school and high-latitude codes listed in the `query` comment above each
# group. This is a build-time step and never a runtime one: the theme makes no network call,
# ever, and this file is why it does not have to.
#
# The `ours` column is `=` where our answer is the oracle's, and the six values we produce
# otherwise. Every disagreement is annotated below with the reason and with a third opinion
# from an independent high-precision solar position (the NOAA/Meeus algorithm, roughly a
# hundred times finer than the approximation both we and the oracle use). We are not the
# arbiter of our own correctness: where we differ from the oracle, something outside both of us
# was asked.
#
# COVERAGE
#
#   latitudes      21°N to 78°N and 34°S to 55°S, both hemispheres
#   seasons        both solstices, an equinox, and dates well away from either
#   asr            both schools, at two latitudes
#   isha           angle form and fixed-interval form
#   high latitude  all three conventions on the same day and place, so they can be compared
#   DST            both United States transition days, in a zone that observes them
#   no solution    midnight sun and polar night, where the honest answer is that there is none
#
# FORMAT — one row per line, fields separated by `|`:
#
#   id | epoch | lat | lon | tz | compute arguments | oracle six | ours six or `=`
#
# The six values are fajr, sunrise, dhuhr, asr, maghrib, isha as local civil `HH:MM` in the
# row's zone, or `none` for a prayer that does not occur. The epoch is UTC seconds at local noon
# on the day in question — an arbitrary instant inside the right day, which is the whole point:
# the calculation is handed a moment, never a clock.

# query: method=3 (Muslim World League, fajr 18 / isha 17), school 0 and 1, ANGLE_BASED
# The anchor. Every one of the six matches, in both schools, which is the row every other row is
# read against.
algiers-mwl-shafi | 1785150000 | 36.7538 | 3.0588 | Africa/Algiers | fajr_angle=18 isha_angle=17 | 04:06 05:49 12:54 16:44 19:59 21:35 | =
algiers-mwl-hanafi | 1785150000 | 36.7538 | 3.0588 | Africa/Algiers | fajr_angle=18 isha_angle=17 asr_factor=2 | 04:06 05:49 12:54 17:53 19:59 21:35 | =

# query: method=19 (Algeria, fajr 18 / isha 17)
# Same angles as MWL by publication, so this row proves the table entry and not the arithmetic.
algiers-algeria | 1785150000 | 36.7538 | 3.0588 | Africa/Algiers | fajr_angle=18 isha_angle=17 | 04:06 05:49 12:54 16:44 19:59 21:35 | =

# query: method=4 (Umm al-Qura, fajr 18.5 / isha 90 min after maghrib)
# The interval form of isha, at both solstices and at an equinox. `mecca-ummalqura-jun` misses
# dhuhr by one minute and it is a rounding tie, not an error: the high-precision answer is
# 12:22:29.7, the oracle rounds 12:22, and our approximation lands at 12:22:30.4 — three
# tenths of a second past the boundary, well inside the arithmetic's own error. Kept rather
# than replaced with a comfortable date, because a matrix that only holds easy days proves less.
mecca-ummalqura-jun | 1782032400 | 21.4225 | 39.8262 | Asia/Riyadh | fajr_angle=18.5 isha_interval=90 | 04:11 05:39 12:22 15:42 19:06 20:36 | 04:11 05:39 12:23 15:42 19:06 20:36
mecca-ummalqura-dec | 1797843600 | 21.4225 | 39.8262 | Asia/Riyadh | fajr_angle=18.5 isha_interval=90 | 05:32 06:54 12:19 15:23 17:44 19:14 | =
mecca-ummalqura-hanafi | 1773997200 | 21.4225 | 39.8262 | Asia/Riyadh | fajr_angle=18.5 isha_interval=90 asr_factor=2 | 05:09 06:25 12:28 16:50 18:32 20:02 | =

# query: method=5 (Egyptian General Authority of Survey, fajr 19.5 / isha 17.5)
# asr differs by one minute. Independent high-precision answer 15:29:42, which rounds to our
# 15:30 rather than to the oracle's 15:29.
cairo-egyptian-equinox | 1774000800 | 30.0444 | 31.2357 | Africa/Cairo | fajr_angle=19.5 isha_angle=17.5 | 04:32 05:59 12:03 15:29 18:06 19:24 | 04:32 05:59 12:03 15:30 18:06 19:24

# query: method=1 (University of Islamic Sciences, Karachi, fajr 18 / isha 18)
# asr differs by two minutes — the largest disagreement in this file. Independent high-precision
# answer 15:50:30, two seconds from ours and ninety from the oracle's. A year of this location
# checked day by day puts the oracle's asr on an annual wobble of about ±1.5 minutes against
# both us and the precise ephemeris, while its other five prayers agree with us on 365 days out
# of 365. The disagreement is in the oracle's asr, and it is bounded.
karachi-karachi-equinox | 1790146800 | 24.8607 | 67.0011 | Asia/Karachi | fajr_angle=18 isha_angle=18 | 05:05 06:21 12:24 15:52 18:28 19:44 | 05:05 06:21 12:24 15:50 18:28 19:44

# query: method=2 (ISNA, fajr 15 / isha 15)
# The two days a year the zone's offset changes. Nothing in the calculation knows: every answer
# is an instant, and the offset is applied by strftime at the last possible moment. asr differs
# by a minute on each, in opposite directions, and the high-precision answers — 16:21:50 and
# 14:28:28 — are ours.
newyork-isna-dst-start | 1772985600 | 40.7128 | -74.006 | America/New_York | fajr_angle=15 isha_angle=15 | 06:04 07:19 13:07 16:21 18:55 20:10 | 06:04 07:19 13:07 16:22 18:55 20:10
newyork-isna-dst-end | 1793552400 | 40.7128 | -74.006 | America/New_York | fajr_angle=15 isha_angle=15 | 05:10 06:26 11:40 14:30 16:52 18:09 | 05:10 06:26 11:40 14:29 16:52 18:09

# query: method=3, ANGLE_BASED — the southern hemisphere, where summer and winter are the other
# way round and a naive sign error would show up immediately.
sydney-mwl-dec | 1797814800 | -33.8688 | 151.2093 | Australia/Sydney | fajr_angle=18 isha_angle=17 | 03:56 05:41 12:53 16:38 20:05 21:43 | =
capetown-mwl-jun | 1782036000 | -33.9249 | 18.4241 | Africa/Johannesburg | fajr_angle=18 isha_angle=17 | 06:22 07:51 12:48 15:27 17:45 19:09 | =
buenosaires-mwl-dec | 1797865200 | -34.6037 | -58.3816 | America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires | fajr_angle=18 isha_angle=17 | 03:51 05:37 12:52 16:38 20:06 21:45 | =

# query: method=3 with latitudeAdjustmentMethod 3, 2 and 1 — one place, one day, three
# conventions. At 64°N in June the sun sets but never reaches 18° below the horizon, so fajr and
# isha are portions of the night in every row; sunrise, dhuhr, asr and maghrib are identical
# across all three, which is what says the convention touches only the two prayers it should.
# Maghrib and isha fall after local midnight and are reported as the next day's clock time.
reykjavik-angle | 1782043200 | 64.1466 | -21.9426 | Atlantic/Reykjavik | fajr_angle=18 isha_angle=17 highlat=angle | 02:04 02:55 13:30 18:23 00:04 00:52 | =
reykjavik-seventh | 1782043200 | 64.1466 | -21.9426 | Atlantic/Reykjavik | fajr_angle=18 isha_angle=17 highlat=seventh | 02:31 02:55 13:30 18:23 00:04 00:28 | =
reykjavik-middle | 1782043200 | 64.1466 | -21.9426 | Atlantic/Reykjavik | fajr_angle=18 isha_angle=17 highlat=middle | 01:30 02:55 13:30 18:23 00:04 01:30 | =

# query: method=3, ANGLE_BASED — the southern equivalent, in high-latitude summer.
ushuaia-angle-dec | 1797865200 | -54.8019 | -68.303 | America/Argentina/Ushuaia | fajr_angle=18 isha_angle=17 highlat=angle | 02:51 04:51 13:31 18:01 22:11 00:05 | =

# query: method=3, ANGLE_BASED — the two rows this file exists for.
#
# `svalbard-midnight-sun`: at 78°N in June the sun never crosses the horizon at all. There is no
# sunrise, no sunset, and therefore no night to take a portion of, so fajr, sunrise, maghrib and
# isha have no answer. The oracle reports 00:59 for all four — a number, of the right shape, on
# the right day, and meaningless. We report `none`, and this row is the deliberate divergence
# the sentinel exists for. Dhuhr and asr are real and we agree on both: the sun still crosses
# the meridian, and it still casts a shadow.
#
# `svalbard-polar-night`: the same place in December, where the sun never rises but does climb
# to within 12° of the horizon — so fajr and isha, measured at 18° and 17° below it, do occur,
# while sunrise and maghrib do not. That asymmetry is the point: absence is decided per prayer,
# from the arithmetic, and not from the latitude.
#
# Asr diverges here for a third reason again. Its rule measures a shadow against the one an
# object casts at noon, and under a polar night there is no noon shadow to measure against. The
# arithmetic still yields a number — the rule degenerates rather than failing — and the oracle
# reports it as 14:46. It is a time of day at which nothing happens, so we report `none`. Note
# that the June row above keeps its asr: there the sun never sets, which is a different thing
# entirely, and a shadow it casts all day is still a shadow.
svalbard-midnight-sun | 1782036000 | 78.2232 | 15.6267 | Arctic/Longyearbyen | fajr_angle=18 isha_angle=17 highlat=angle | 00:59 00:59 12:59 19:08 00:59 00:59 | none none 12:59 19:08 none none
svalbard-polar-night | 1797850800 | 78.2232 | 15.6267 | Arctic/Longyearbyen | fajr_angle=18 isha_angle=17 highlat=angle | 07:37 11:55 11:56 14:46 11:56 15:51 | 07:37 none 11:56 none none 15:51
